title: The Salt Market
description: A harbor week: a stuck gate, a missing barrel, a wreck with a name, and a charter the council will not spend oil on.
premise: Nothing lands at the salt market until someone writes it down, and the one wreck that matters was never written down.
tone: Damp stone, lamp oil, argument over paper
themes: Records against what the water keeps, duty, the price of a landing
writing_style: Close third, concrete work, short scenes

entities.notes: Harbormaster. She keeps the gate and the bell.

assertions.statement: The bell and the ovens start the day together.
The gate opens only after the bell has had its say.
Ivo's signature is the landing the charter describes.
The missing barrel is the count Holm would not round.
The landing tax is an argument about salt.
The road closes because of what the dive found.
The Sable reaches the council as a name, not a hull.
Refusing the oil is how the council answers the bell.
One sounding is written in the ledger and the archive.
Ness writes the landing before Ivo will sign it.
The charter is carried to the gate it governs.
The skiff and the salt end in the same warehouse.
The night shift eats because Holm's count runs long.
Pell warns Jun off the road Jun sounded from.
The Kestrel gets in only when the gate decides to lift.
The posted price and the argued tax are the same salt.
The copy Ness files is the charter Bram read.
The diver's report is how the wreck enters the charter's week.
The shut gate is a landing fact because Ness wrote it.
The bell reaches Oven Row, and the ovens answer.
The archive keeps the depths the dive was made in.
Ivo refuses the tide and still signs the landing.
Jun is paid out of the salt he did not carry.
The road is closed after the one walk Bram takes.
The custom house holds the landing and the charter's copy.
The light skiff is the end of Ani's dive.
The market hears the tax in the afternoon price.
Pell copies a sounding he did not take.
